Read and write Xper2 / Xper3 knowledge bases

Source: R/sdd.R
readXper.Rd

Xper3 (and its desktop predecessor Xper2) keep a knowledge base of taxa ("items") described by characters ("descriptors"). Their documented interchange format is SDD: export the knowledge base as SDD from Xper, and import an SDD file written by writeXper() there. Xper's own storage format is not publicly specified, so dimoose does not try to read or write it; these two functions read and write the SDD dialect that Xper produces.

Usage

readXper(file, taxon = "Taxon", sep = "/", inapplicable = NA, strict = TRUE)

writeXper(
  x,
  file,
  characters = NULL,
  taxon = "Taxon",
  title = NULL,
  sep = "/",
  inapplicable = NULL,
  lang = "en"
)

Arguments

file

Path of the SDD file to read or write.

taxon

Name of the taxon column of the matrix.

sep

Separator between the states of a variable taxon in one cell.

inapplicable

For readers, the cell value to give "not applicable" (default NA, the same as unknown). For writers, the cell value that means "not applicable" (default NULL: none).

strict

If TRUE, stop when the file does not say it was generated by Xper.

x

A character matrix (data frame), or the list returned by readSDD(), readDELTA(), readLucid() or readXper().

characters

Optional data frame describing the characters: a Character column matching the matrix's column names and any of Type, States (to fix the order of the states or list states no taxon has), Unit, InapplicableIf and Cost. By default taken from x if x is a reader's result; otherwise numeric columns are written as numeric characters and all others as categorical ones.

title

Title of the dataset; by default the title in the metadata of x.

lang

Language of the labels, as an xml:lang code.

Value

readXper() returns the same tdwgData list as readSDD(); writeXper() returns file, invisibly.

Details

Compared with plain readSDD(), the Xper dialect has a few habits that are handled here: Xper2 names each taxon in the label of its coded description rather than in a taxon list; the dependencies between characters are InapplicableIf rules in a single character tree; and every coding carries an observation-convenience rating, which is read as the character's Cost (1 = easy to 5 = hard). readXper() stops if the file was not written by Xper, unless strict = FALSE.

References

Vignes-Lebbe, R., Chesselet, P. & Diep Thi, M.-H. (2016). Xper3: new tools for collaborating, training and transmitting knowledge on botanical phenotypes. In: Botanists of the twenty-first century, UNESCO. https://www.xper3.fr/

See also

readSDD(), writeSDD().

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "tdwg", "felids-xper3.sdd.xml", package = "dimoose")
d <- readXper(f)
d$matrix
#>              Taxon  Coat pattern Shape of the spots            Claws
#> 1     Panthera leo         plain               <NA> fully retractile
#> 2  Panthera tigris       striped               <NA> fully retractile
#> 3  Panthera pardus plain/spotted           rosettes fully retractile
#> 4 Acinonyx jubatus       spotted        solid spots  semi-retractile
#>   Mane in adult males
#> 1             present
#> 2              absent
#> 3              absent
#> 4                <NA>
d$characters[, c("Character", "InapplicableIf", "Cost")]
#>             Character             InapplicableIf Cost
#> 1        Coat pattern                               1
#> 2  Shape of the spots Coat pattern=plain/striped    3
#> 3               Claws                               4
#> 4 Mane in adult males                               2

out <- writeXper(d, tempfile(fileext = ".sdd.xml"))
identical(readXper(out)$matrix, d$matrix)
#> [1] TRUE
